\section{Diagonalization --- Ladner}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.Complexity.Diagonalization.Ladner
This module develops Ladner's theorem by delayed diagonalization: it pads SAT by a
slowly growing index function $H$, defined as the least machine index that correctly
recognises the padded language on short inputs within its indexed polynomial clock,
and shows that the padded language $\mathrm{SAT}_H$ is neither in $\mathsf{P}$ nor
$\mathsf{NP}$-hard when $\mathsf{P}\ne\mathsf{NP}$. It also supplies the padding parser,
the shrinking argument that turns a reduction from SAT into a polynomial-time decider,
and the polynomial-time preparation of the bounded candidate test.

\begin{definition}[Padded SAT language]
\lean{Complexity.padSAT}
\label{Complexity.padSAT}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT}
For a function $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, the padded language $\mathrm{SAT}_h$ is the set
of Boolean strings of the form $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$:
a satisfiable encoded formula, followed by a single separator bit $0$, followed by
$|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}$ ones.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in padded SAT]
\lean{Complexity.mem_padSAT_iff}
\label{Complexity.mem_padSAT_iff}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT, Complexity.padSAT}
\difficulty{1}
For every function $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and every Boolean string $y$, the string $y$
belongs to the padded language $\mathrm{SAT}_h$ if and only if there is $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$
with $y=\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Padded membership depends on shorter exponents]
\lean{Complexity.padSAT_congr}
\label{Complexity.padSAT_congr}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.mem_padSAT_iff, Complexity.padSAT}
\difficulty{3}
For functions $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, let $\mathrm{SAT}_h$ be the set of strings
$\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$. Let $h,g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$
and let $y$ be a Boolean string such that $h(m)=g(m)$ for every $m<|y|$. Then
$y\in\mathrm{SAT}_h$ if and only if $y\in\mathrm{SAT}_g$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Ladner's machine enumeration]
\lean{Complexity.ladnerMachine}
\label{Complexity.ladnerMachine}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.expCode, Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM, Turing.FinTM}
For $i\in\mathbb N$, the machine $M_i$ is the finite-state Boolean Turing machine obtained
by decoding the little-endian binary digits of $i$ with a fixed uniform machine code for
one-work-tape Boolean machines (a code whose decoded machines admit a uniformly clocked
simulator).
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Unfolding the machine enumeration]
\lean{Complexity.ladnerMachine_eq}
\label{Complexity.ladnerMachine_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.expCode, Complexity.ladnerMachine, Turing.CodeTM.toFinTM}
\difficulty{1}
For every $i\in\mathbb N$, the $i$-th machine $M_i$ of Ladner's enumeration equals the
finite-state Boolean machine obtained by decoding the binary digits of $i$ with the fixed
uniform machine code.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Ladner's delayed index function]
\lean{Complexity.ladnerH}
\label{Complexity.ladnerH}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladnerMachine, Complexity.padSAT, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
Write $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$), let $M_i$ be the machine decoded
from the binary digits of $i$, and say that $M$ accepts $x$ within $t$ steps if it halts
within $t$ steps with output the single bit $1$. The function $H:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ is
defined by strong recursion: $H(n)$ is the least $i<\ell(\ell(n))$ such that for every
Boolean string $x$ with $|x|\le\ell(n)$, $M_i$ accepts $x$ within $i\,|x|^i$ steps if and
only if $x\in\mathrm{SAT}_{H'}$, where $H'$ agrees with $H$ below $n$ and is $0$ elsewhere;
if no such $i$ exists, $H(n)=\ell(\ell(n))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Defining equation of the delayed index]
\lean{Complexity.ladnerH_eq}
\label{Complexity.ladnerH_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladnerH, Complexity.ladnerMachine, Complexity.padSAT, Complexity.padSAT_congr, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
\difficulty{5}
Let $H$ be Ladner's delayed index function, $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$, $M_i$ the
machine decoded from the binary digits of $i$, and $\mathrm{SAT}_H$ the strings
$\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{H(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$. For every $n$, $H(n)$ is the
least $i<\ell(\ell(n))$ such that for every Boolean string $x$ with $|x|\le\ell(n)$, $M_i$
halts within $i\,|x|^i$ steps with output $1$ if and only if $x\in\mathrm{SAT}_H$; if no
such $i$ exists, $H(n)=\ell(\ell(n))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Double-logarithmic cap on the delayed index]
\lean{Complexity.ladnerH_le}
\label{Complexity.ladnerH_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladnerH, Complexity.ladnerH_eq}
\difficulty{3}
Let $H$ be Ladner's delayed index function. For every $n\in\mathbb N$,
$H(n)\le\lfloor\log_2\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor\rfloor$ (with $\log_2 0$ read as $0$).
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[The Ladner language]
\lean{Complexity.SAT_H}
\label{Complexity.SAT_H}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladnerH, Complexity.padSAT}
The language $\mathrm{SAT}_H$ is SAT padded by Ladner's delayed index function $H$: it
consists of the strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{H(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Unfolding the Ladner language]
\lean{Complexity.SAT_H_eq}
\label{Complexity.SAT_H_eq}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT_H, Complexity.ladnerH, Complexity.padSAT}
\difficulty{1}
Let $H$ be Ladner's delayed index function. The Ladner language $\mathrm{SAT}_H$ equals the
padded language of all strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{H(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Empty word is never padded]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_pad_nil}
\label{Complexity.ladner_pad_nil}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.mem_padSAT_iff, Complexity.padSAT}
\difficulty{3}
For every function $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, the empty string does not belong to the padded
language $\mathrm{SAT}_h=\{\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}:\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Prepending bits to a binary expansion]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_bits_prepend}
\label{Complexity.ladner_bits_prepend}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $u$ be a Boolean string and $j>0$ a natural number. Then there is a natural number
$i\ge j$ whose little-endian binary expansion is $u$ followed by the binary expansion of $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Every machine has arbitrarily large indices]

\label{Complexity.ladner_padded_index}
\leanok

\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Padding parser]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_parse}
\label{Complexity.ladner_parse}
\leanok
The padding parser takes a Boolean string $y$. If $y$ contains a $0$, it returns the pair
$(p,t)$ with $y=p\,0\,1^t$, where $p$ is the prefix before the last $0$ of $y$ and $t$ is
the number of ones after it; if $y$ contains no $0$, it fails.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Padding syntax test]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_padSyntax}
\label{Complexity.ladner_padSyntax}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_parse}
For a function $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and a Boolean string $y$, the padding syntax test
is the bit that is $1$ exactly when $y$ can be written as $p\,0\,1^t$ (with $p$ the prefix
before the last $0$) and $t=|p|^{h(|p|)}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Serialized padding parse]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_parseWord}
\label{Complexity.ladner_parseWord}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_parse, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ denote the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings and
$\mathrm{bin}(t)$ the binary expansion of $t$. For a Boolean string $y$, the serialized
parse is the empty string if $y$ contains no $0$, and otherwise is
$\langle 1,\langle p,\mathrm{bin}(t)\rangle\rangle$, where $y=p\,0\,1^t$ with $p$ the
prefix before the last $0$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Parser fails exactly on all-ones words]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_parse_none}
\label{Complexity.ladner_parse_none}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_parse}
\difficulty{4}
For every Boolean string $y$, the padding parser (which splits $y$ as $p\,0\,1^t$ at its
last $0$) fails on $y$ if and only if every bit of $y$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Soundness of the padding parser]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_parse_sound}
\label{Complexity.ladner_parse_sound}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_parse, Complexity.ladner_parse_none}
\difficulty{5}
Let $y,p$ be Boolean strings and $t\in\mathbb N$. If the padding parser, which splits a
string at its last $0$, returns $(p,t)$ on $y$, then $y=p\,0\,1^t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Parser reads padded words]

\begin{theorem}[Characterization of successful parses]

\begin{theorem}[Length of a parsed word]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_parsed_length}
\label{Complexity.ladner_parsed_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_parse, Complexity.ladner_parse_some}

Let $y,p$ be Boolean strings and $t\in\mathbb N$. If the padding parser, which splits a
string at its last $0$, returns $(p,t)$ on $y$, then $|y|=|p|+1+t$ and $|p|<|y|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero-bit test is false on all-ones words]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_hasFalse_false}
\label{Complexity.ladner_hasFalse_false}
\leanok

\difficulty{3}
For a Boolean string $y$, let $z(y)$ be the bit that is $1$ exactly when $y$ contains a
$0$. Then $z(y)=0$ if and only if every bit of $y$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Zero-bit test distributes over concatenation]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_hasFalse_append}
\label{Complexity.ladner_hasFalse_append}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.hasFalse, Complexity.BinArith.hasFalse_cons, Complexity.BinArith.hasFalse_nil}
\difficulty{3}
For a Boolean string $y$, let $z(y)$ be the bit that is $1$ exactly when $y$ contains a
$0$. For all Boolean strings $u,v$, $z(uv)=z(u)\vee z(v)$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Complexity.ladner_parse_prefix}
\label{Complexity.ladner_parse_prefix}

\difficulty{3}

\lean{Complexity.ladner_padSyntax_FP}

\begin{theorem}[Padding syntax test is polynomial-time]

\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.ladner_padSyntax, Complexity.ladner_padSyntax_FP, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_id, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD}

Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be such that the map $x\mapsto\mathrm{bin}(h(|x|))$, sending a
Boolean string to the binary expansion of $h$ at its length, is polynomial-time computable.
Then the map sending a Boolean string $y$ to the bit that is $1$ exactly when $y=p\,0\,1^t$
with $p$ the prefix before the last $0$ and $t=|p|^{h(|p|)}$ is computable in polynomial
time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Padded membership via the parser]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_pad_membership}
\label{Complexity.ladner_pad_membership}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT, Complexity.ladner_parse, Complexity.ladner_parse_some, Complexity.mem_padSAT_iff, Complexity.padSAT}
\difficulty{3}
Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and let $\mathrm{SAT}_h$ be the set of strings
$\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$. A Boolean string $y$ lies in
$\mathrm{SAT}_h$ if and only if the padding parser (splitting at the last $0$) returns some
$(p,t)$ on $y$ with $t=|p|^{h(|p|)}$ and $p\in\mathrm{SAT}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Finite tables are polynomial-time]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_finite_lookup_FP}
\label{Complexity.ladner_finite_lookup_FP}
\leanok

For every finite set $S$ of Boolean strings, the map sending a Boolean string $x$ to the
bit that is $1$ exactly when $x\in S$ is computable in polynomial time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Short SAT instances form a finite table]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_small_SAT_table}
\label{Complexity.ladner_small_SAT_table}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT}
\difficulty{4}
For every $B\in\mathbb N$ there is a finite set $S$ of Boolean strings such that for every
Boolean string $x$, $x\in S$ if and only if $|x|<B$ and $x\in\mathrm{SAT}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Short-input SAT bit]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_smallSAT}
\label{Complexity.ladner_smallSAT}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT}
For $B\in\mathbb N$ and a Boolean string $x$, the short-input SAT bit is $1$ exactly when
$|x|<B$ and $x\in\mathrm{SAT}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One shrinking round]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_parse, Complexity.ladner_smallSAT, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with
components $\pi_1(S),\pi_2(S)$ of a string $S$, and for a property $Q$ let $[Q]$ be the bit
that is $1$ exactly when $Q$ holds. For $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, a string function $f$ and
$B,K\in\mathbb N$, the shrinking round sends a state $S$ to $S$ itself if $\pi_1(S)$ is
nonempty; otherwise, with $x=\pi_2(S)$, it returns $\langle[\,|x|<K\wedge x\in\mathrm{SAT}\,],
\varepsilon\rangle$ if $|x|<K$; $\langle 0,\varepsilon\rangle$ if $f(x)$ contains no $0$, or
if $f(x)=p\,0\,1^t$ (split at the last $0$) with $t\ne|p|^{h(|p|)}$; and otherwise
$\langle[\,|p|<B\wedge p\in\mathrm{SAT}\,],\varepsilon\rangle$ if $|p|<B$ and
$\langle\varepsilon,p\rangle$ if $|p|\ge B$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Shrinking invariant]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_ShrinkInv}
\label{Complexity.ladner_ShrinkInv}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings. For Boolean
strings $x$ and $S$, the shrinking invariant holds when either $S=\langle\varepsilon,y\rangle$
for some string $y$ with $|y|\le|x|$ and $y\in\mathrm{SAT}\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$, or
$S=\langle b,\varepsilon\rangle$ for a single bit $b$ with $b=1\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Shrinking measure]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrinkMeasure}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrinkMeasure}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $\pi_1(S),\pi_2(S)$ be the components of a Boolean string $S$ decoded as a
self-delimiting pair (empty if $S$ is not a pair). The shrinking measure of $S$ is
$\mu(S)=|\pi_2(S)|+1$ if $\pi_1(S)$ is empty, and $\mu(S)=0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[NP-hardness supplies a reduction from SAT]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_reduction_from_hardness}
\label{Complexity.ladner_reduction_from_hardness}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NPHard, Complexity.NPHard_iff, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.SAT, Complexity.SAT_mem_NP, Complexity.padSAT, Complexity.polyTimeReducible_iff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and let $\mathrm{SAT}_h$ be the set of strings
$\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$. If $\mathrm{SAT}_h$ is
$\mathsf{NP}$-hard, then there is a polynomial-time computable string function $f$ such that
$x\in\mathrm{SAT}\iff f(x)\in\mathrm{SAT}_h$ for every Boolean string $x$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Large exponents force short prefixes]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_prefix_square_bound}
\label{Complexity.ladner_prefix_square_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and $A,d,B,n,m\in\mathbb N$. Suppose $h(r)\ge 2(d+1)$ for all
$r\ge B$, $n\ge A\,2^d+2$, $m\ge B$, and $m^{h(m)}\le A\,(n+1)^d$. Then $m^2\le n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Reductions into padded SAT shrink prefixes]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_reduction_shrinks}
\label{Complexity.ladner_reduction_shrinks}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.output_length_le, Complexity.ladner_parse, Complexity.ladner_parsed_length, Complexity.ladner_prefix_square_bound}
\difficulty{5}
Let $f$ be a polynomial-time computable string function and $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ a
function such that for every $C$ there is $N$ with $C\le h(n)$ for all $n\ge N$. Then there
are $B$ and $K\ge 2$ such that for all Boolean strings $x,p$ and $t\in\mathbb N$: if
$|x|\ge K$, $f(x)=p\,0\,1^t$ (split at the last $0$), $t=|p|^{h(|p|)}$ and $|p|\ge B$, then
$|p|^2\le|x|$ and $|p|<|x|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Short-input SAT bit is polynomial-time]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_smallSAT_FP}
\label{Complexity.ladner_smallSAT_FP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.ladner_finite_lookup_FP, Complexity.ladner_smallSAT, Complexity.ladner_small_SAT_table}
\difficulty{3}
For every $B\in\mathbb N$, the map sending a Boolean string $x$ to the bit that is $1$
exactly when $|x|<B$ and $x\in\mathrm{SAT}$ is computable in polynomial time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A shrinking round is polynomial-time]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep_FP}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep_FP}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.lt_pairEncode, Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_lt, Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_slot2, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode, Complexity.ladner_lengthBits_FP, Complexity.ladner_padSyntax, Complexity.ladner_parse, Complexity.ladner_parseWord, Complexity.ladner_parse_FP, Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep, Complexity.ladner_smallSAT_FP, Complexity.ladner_syntax_FP, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_const, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_id, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_isNil, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_ite, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairSndD, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be such that $x\mapsto\mathrm{bin}(h(|x|))$ is polynomial-time
computable, let $f$ be a polynomial-time computable string function, and let
$B,K\in\mathbb N$. Then the shrinking round is polynomial-time computable; here, writing
$\langle u,v\rangle$ for pairing with components $\pi_1,\pi_2$ and $[Q]$ for the truth bit
of $Q$, the round fixes $S$ when $\pi_1(S)\ne\varepsilon$ and otherwise, with
$x=\pi_2(S)$, returns $\langle[x\in\mathrm{SAT}],\varepsilon\rangle$ if $|x|<K$,
$\langle 0,\varepsilon\rangle$ unless $f(x)=p\,0\,1^t$ with $t=|p|^{h(|p|)}$, and then
$\langle[p\in\mathrm{SAT}],\varepsilon\rangle$ if $|p|<B$ and $\langle\varepsilon,p\rangle$
otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Correct terminal answers respect the shrinking ledger]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrink_terminal_result}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrink_terminal_result}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT, Complexity.ladner_ShrinkInv, Complexity.ladner_shrinkMeasure, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, let
$\mu(\langle\varepsilon,y\rangle)=|y|+1$ and $\mu(\langle b,\varepsilon\rangle)=0$ for a bit
$b$, and say that the invariant holds for $(x,S)$ when either $S=\langle\varepsilon,y\rangle$
with $|y|\le|x|$ and $y\in\mathrm{SAT}\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$, or $S=\langle b,\varepsilon\rangle$
with $b=1\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$. Let $x,y$ be strings and $b$ a bit with
$b=1\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$. Then the invariant holds for $(x,\langle b,\varepsilon\rangle)$;
if $\mu(\langle\varepsilon,y\rangle)>0$ then $\mu(\langle b,\varepsilon\rangle)<
\mu(\langle\varepsilon,y\rangle)$; and if $\mu(\langle\varepsilon,y\rangle)=0$ then
$\langle b,\varepsilon\rangle=\langle\varepsilon,y\rangle$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A shrinking round makes progress]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrink_progress}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrink_progress}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT, Complexity.ladner_ShrinkInv, Complexity.ladner_pad_membership, Complexity.ladner_parse, Complexity.ladner_shrinkMeasure, Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep, Complexity.ladner_shrink_terminal_result, Complexity.ladner_smallSAT, Complexity.padSAT, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{6}
Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, let $f$ be a string function with
$x\in\mathrm{SAT}\iff f(x)\in\mathrm{SAT}_h$ for all $x$ (where $\mathrm{SAT}_h$ is the set of
strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$), and let $B,K$ with
$K\ge 2$ be such that $|p|<|x|$ whenever $|x|\ge K$, $f(x)=p\,0\,1^t$ (split at the last $0$),
$t=|p|^{h(|p|)}$ and $|p|\ge B$. Let $\sigma$ be the shrinking round for $h,f,B,K$, $\mu$ the
shrinking measure ($|\pi_2(S)|+1$ if $\pi_1(S)$ is empty, else $0$) and $I_x$ the shrinking
invariant ($S=\langle\varepsilon,y\rangle$ with $|y|\le|x|$ and the same SAT answer as $x$,
or $S=\langle b,\varepsilon\rangle$ with $b=1\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$). Then for all strings
$x,S$ with $I_x(S)$: $I_x(\sigma(S))$ holds, $\mu(\sigma(S))<\mu(S)$ whenever $\mu(S)>0$, and
$\sigma(S)=S$ whenever $\mu(S)=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Initial shrinking state satisfies the invariant]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrink_initial}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrink_initial}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_ShrinkInv, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings. For every
Boolean string $x$, the state $\langle\varepsilon,x\rangle$ satisfies the shrinking
invariant for $x$: there is $y$ with $\langle\varepsilon,x\rangle=\langle\varepsilon,y\rangle$,
$|y|\le|x|$, and $y\in\mathrm{SAT}\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Linear size bound along the shrinking orbit]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrink_orbit_size}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrink_orbit_size}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.iterate_invariant, Complexity.ladner_ShrinkInv, Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep, Complexity.ladner_shrink_initial, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{4}
Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, $f$ a string function, $B,K\in\mathbb N$, and $\sigma$ the
shrinking round for $h,f,B,K$. For strings $x,S$, let $I_x(S)$ be the shrinking invariant:
$S=\langle\varepsilon,y\rangle$ with $|y|\le|x|$ and $y\in\mathrm{SAT}\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$,
or $S=\langle b,\varepsilon\rangle$ for a bit $b$ with $b=1\iff x\in\mathrm{SAT}$. If
$I_x(S)$ implies $I_x(\sigma(S))$ for all $x,S$, then for every string $x$ and every
$j\in\mathbb N$, $|\sigma^{j}(\langle\varepsilon,x\rangle)|\le 4(|x|+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Shrinking orbit ends with the SAT answer]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrink_final_readout}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrink_final_readout}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.iterate_invariant, Complexity.BinArith.iterate_measure_eq_zero, Complexity.SAT, Complexity.ladner_ShrinkInv, Complexity.ladner_shrinkMeasure, Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep, Complexity.ladner_shrink_initial, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, $f$ a string function, $B,K\in\mathbb N$, $\sigma$ the
shrinking round for $h,f,B,K$, $\mu$ the shrinking measure ($|\pi_2(S)|+1$ if $\pi_1(S)$ is
empty, else $0$) and $I_x$ the shrinking invariant for $x$. Suppose that for all strings
$x,S$ with $I_x(S)$, $I_x(\sigma(S))$ holds, $\mu(\sigma(S))<\mu(S)$ whenever $\mu(S)>0$, and
$\sigma(S)=S$ whenever $\mu(S)=0$. Then for every string $x$, the first component of
$\sigma^{|x|+1}(\langle\varepsilon,x\rangle)$ is the one-bit string that is $1$ exactly when
$x\in\mathrm{SAT}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Shrinking puts SAT in P]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shrinking_transfer}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shrinking_transfer}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_iterate, Complexity.P, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode, Complexity.SAT, Complexity.ladner_shrinkStep, Complexity.mem_P_of_test, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_const, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_id, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD, Turing.pairEncode}

Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$, $f$ a string function, $B,K\in\mathbb N$, and $\sigma$ the
shrinking round for $h,f,B,K$, with $\langle u,v\rangle$ the pairing and $\pi_1$ its first
component. Suppose $\sigma$ is polynomial-time computable,
$|\sigma^{j}(\langle\varepsilon,x\rangle)|\le 4(|x|+1)$ for every string $x$ and every
$j\le|x|+1$, and $\pi_1(\sigma^{|x|+1}(\langle\varepsilon,x\rangle))$ is the one-bit string
that is $1$ exactly when $x\in\mathrm{SAT}$, for every $x$. Then $\mathrm{SAT}\in\mathsf{P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Numeric memo values]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_values}
\label{Complexity.ladner_values}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.decWords, Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal}
For a Boolean string $T$, decode $T$ as a list of strings by repeatedly taking the first
component of a self-delimiting pair and continuing with the second component until the
remainder is empty; the memo values of $T$ are the natural numbers whose little-endian
binary expansions are these strings, in order.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Enumeration of short words]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shortWords}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shortWords}
\leanok
For every $a\in\mathbb N$, the short-word list of $a$ is the list whose entries are, for
$r=0,1,\dots,2^{a+1}-2$ in order, the little-endian binary expansion of $r+1$ with its last
(most significant) bit deleted.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Stage selection from memo values]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_stage}
\label{Complexity.ladner_stage}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladnerMachine, Complexity.padSAT, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
Let $v=(v_0,\dots,v_{n-1})$ be a list of natural numbers of length $n$, write
$\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$), let $M_i$ be the machine decoded from
the binary digits of $i$, and let $\mathrm{SAT}_v$ be SAT padded by the exponent function
$m\mapsto v_m$ (read as $0$ for $m\ge n$). The stage value of $v$ is the least
$i<\ell(\ell(n))$ such that for every Boolean string $x$ with $|x|\le\ell(n)$, $M_i$ halts
within $i\,|x|^i$ steps with output $1$ if and only if $x\in\mathrm{SAT}_v$; if no such $i$
exists, it is $\ell(\ell(n))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Candidate index test]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_candidate}
\label{Complexity.ladner_candidate}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.ladnerMachine, Complexity.ladner_values, Complexity.padSAT, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
Let $\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the components of a self-delimiting pair, $\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of
a little-endian binary word, $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$, and $M_i$ the machine decoded
from the binary digits of $i$. For a string $S$ put $n=|\pi_1(S)|$,
$i=\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(S)))$ and $v$ the memo values of $\pi_2(\pi_2(S))$. The candidate
bit of $S$ is $1$ exactly when $v$ has length $n$, $i<\ell(\ell(n))$, and for every string $x$
with $|x|\le\ell(n)$, $M_i$ halts within $i\,|x|^i$ steps with output $1$ if and only if $x$
lies in SAT padded by $m\mapsto v_m$ (with $v_m=0$ out of range).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Valid simulator query]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_validQuery}
\label{Complexity.ladner_validQuery}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the components of a self-delimiting pair, $\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of
a little-endian binary word, and $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$. A string $S$ is a valid
query when $\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(S)))<\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(S)|))$ and
$|\pi_2(\pi_2(S))|\le\ell(|\pi_1(S)|)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Code of a guarded query]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_queryCode}
\label{Complexity.ladner_queryCode}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.ladner_validQuery, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the components of a self-delimiting pair, $\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of
a little-endian binary word, $\mathrm{bin}(i)$ the canonical binary expansion of $i$, and
$\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$. For a string $S$, the query code is
$\mathrm{bin}(\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(S))))$ if $\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(S)))<
\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(S)|))$ and $|\pi_2(\pi_2(S))|\le\ell(|\pi_1(S)|)$, and the empty string
otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Input of a guarded query]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_queryInput}
\label{Complexity.ladner_queryInput}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_validQuery, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the components of a self-delimiting pair, $\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of
a little-endian binary word, and $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$. For a string $S$, the
query input is $\pi_2(\pi_2(S))$ if $\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(S)))<\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(S)|))$ and
$|\pi_2(\pi_2(S))|\le\ell(|\pi_1(S)|)$, and the empty string otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Deadline of a guarded query]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_queryDeadline}
\label{Complexity.ladner_queryDeadline}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.ladner_validQuery, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the components of a self-delimiting pair, $\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of
a little-endian binary word, and $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$. For a string $S$ put
$i=\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(S)))$ and $x=\pi_2(\pi_2(S))$. The query deadline is $i\,|x|^i$
if $i<\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(S)|))$ and $|x|\le\ell(|\pi_1(S)|)$, and $0$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Serialized guarded query]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_queryPrep}
\label{Complexity.ladner_queryPrep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_queryCode, Complexity.ladner_queryDeadline, Complexity.ladner_queryInput, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing with components $\pi_1,\pi_2$,
$\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of a little-endian binary word, $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ the binary
expansion of $n$, and $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$. For a string $S$ put
$i=\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(S)))$ and $x=\pi_2(\pi_2(S))$. The serialized query is
$\langle\langle\mathrm{bin}(i\,|x|^i),\mathrm{bin}(i)\rangle,x\rangle$ when
$i<\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(S)|))$ and $|x|\le\ell(|\pi_1(S)|)$, and
$\langle\langle\mathrm{bin}(0),\varepsilon\rangle,\varepsilon\rangle$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Candidate context guard]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_ctxGuard}
\label{Complexity.ladner_ctxGuard}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.ladner_values, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the components of a self-delimiting pair, $\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of
a little-endian binary word, and $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$. A string $C$ passes the
context guard when $|\pi_1(C)|$ equals the number of memo values encoded by
$\pi_2(\pi_2(C))$ and $\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(C)))<\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(C)|))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Verdict on a single ranked word]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_wordVerdict}
\label{Complexity.ladner_wordVerdict}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.bitsVal, Complexity.ladnerMachine, Complexity.ladner_ctxGuard, Complexity.ladner_values, Complexity.padSAT, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.FinTM.ComputesInTime}
Let $\pi_1,\pi_2$ be the components of a self-delimiting pair, $\mathrm{val}(w)$ the value of
a little-endian binary word, $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$, and $M_i$ the machine decoded
from the binary digits of $i$. For a string $C$ and $r\in\mathbb N$, let $x$ be the binary
expansion of $r+1$ with its last bit deleted, $i=\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(C)))$ and $v$ the
memo values of $\pi_2(\pi_2(C))$. The verdict is $1$ exactly when $C$ passes the context
guard ($|\pi_1(C)|$ equals the length of $v$ and $i<\ell(\ell(|\pi_1(C)|))$),
$|x|\le\ell(|\pi_1(C)|)$, and $M_i$ halts within $i\,|x|^i$ steps with output $1$ if and only
if $x$ lies in SAT padded by $m\mapsto v_m$ (with $v_m=0$ out of range).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Number of short-input queries]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_queryCount}
\label{Complexity.ladner_queryCount}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairFstD}
For a Boolean string $C$ with first pair component $\pi_1(C)$, the query count is
$2^{\lfloor\log_2|\pi_1(C)|\rfloor+1}-1$ (with $\log_2 0$ read as $0$).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial state of the candidate scan]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_testInit}
\label{Complexity.ladner_testInit}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_queryCount, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with first
component $\pi_1$. For a string $C$, with $q=2^{\lfloor\log_2|\pi_1(C)|\rfloor+1}-1$, the
initial scan state is $\langle C,\langle 1^{q},\langle\varepsilon,1\rangle\rangle\rangle$,
recording the context, the remaining count in unary, the empty completed rank, and the
conjunction flag $1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One step of the candidate scan]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_testStep}
\label{Complexity.ladner_testStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_wordVerdict, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing with components $\pi_1,\pi_2$. For a
state $S$, put $C=\pi_1(S)$, $m=\pi_1(\pi_2(S))$, $k=\pi_1(\pi_2(\pi_2(S)))$ and
$g=\pi_2(\pi_2(\pi_2(S)))$. If $m$ is empty the step returns $S$; otherwise it returns
$\langle C,\langle m',\langle k1,c\rangle\rangle\rangle$, where $m'$ is $m$ with its first
bit removed, $k1$ is $k$ with a $1$ appended, and $c$ is the one-bit string
$(g_0\wedge V(C,|k|))$, with $g_0$ the first bit of $g$ ($0$ if $g$ is empty) and $V(C,r)$
the single-word verdict of $C$ at rank $r$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Output of the candidate scan]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_testOut}
\label{Complexity.ladner_testOut}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairSndD}
For a Boolean string $S$, with $\pi_2$ the second component of a self-delimiting pair, the
scan output is $\pi_2(\pi_2(\pi_2(S)))$, the conjunction flag of a scan state.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Short-word enumeration is complete]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shortWords_complete}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shortWords_complete}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_le, Complexity.LogProg.lt_two_pow_bits, Complexity.ladner_bits_prepend, Complexity.ladner_shortWords}
\difficulty{5}
For $a\in\mathbb N$, let $W_a$ be the list of the little-endian binary expansions of
$r+1$, with the last bit deleted, for $0\le r\le 2^{a+1}-2$. Then for every Boolean string
$x$, $x$ occurs in $W_a$ if and only if $|x|\le a$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Size of the short-word scan]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_shortWords_count}
\label{Complexity.ladner_shortWords_count}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_shortWords}
\difficulty{3}
For $a\in\mathbb N$, let $W_a$ be the list of the little-endian binary expansions of $r+1$,
with the last bit deleted, for $0\le r\le 2^{a+1}-2$. For every $n\in\mathbb N$, the list
$W_{\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor}$ has length at most $2(n+1)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Squares are bounded by powers of two]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_square_le_power}
\label{Complexity.ladner_square_le_power}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $k$, the square of $k$ is at most $2^{k+1}$, that is,
$k^2\le 2^{k+1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cubic bound on short indexed deadlines]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_short_deadline}
\label{Complexity.ladner_short_deadline}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_square_le_power}
\difficulty{5}
Write $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$). For natural numbers $n,i,m$ with
$i<\ell(\ell(n))$ and $m\le\ell(n)$, we have $i\,m^i\le n^3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Polynomial envelope of the simulation cost]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_numeric_envelope}
\label{Complexity.ladner_numeric_envelope}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_short_deadline, Turing.length_bits_le_self}
\difficulty{4}
Write $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$) and $\mathrm{bin}(i)$ for the
binary expansion of $i$. For natural numbers $D,n,i$ and a Boolean string $x$ with
$i<\ell(\ell(n))$ and $|x|\le\ell(n)$,
\[
  D\,\bigl(|\mathrm{bin}(i)|+|x|+i\,|x|^i+1\bigr)^D\;\le\;D\,4^D\,(n+1)^{3D}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Absorbing a composition clock]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_composition_clock}
\label{Complexity.ladner_composition_clock}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For all natural numbers $C,q,A,e,n$,
\[
  2C\,(n+1)^q+A\,(n+1)^e+2\;\le\;(2C+A+2)\,(n+1)^{\max(q,e)}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Floor logarithm via binary length]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_log_eq_bits_length}
\label{Complexity.ladner_log_eq_bits_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.LogProg.length_bits_eq_log}
\difficulty{3}
For every $n\in\mathbb N$, $\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor=|\mathrm{bin}(n)|-1$, where $\mathrm{bin}(n)$
is the canonical little-endian binary expansion of $n$ (empty for $n=0$), $\lfloor\log_2 0\rfloor$
is read as $0$, and subtraction is truncated at $0$.
\end{theorem}

decides SAT within $b\,2^{m+1}\bigl(a\,(2m+2)^d+(2m+2)^2\bigr)$ steps on every input of length

\begin{definition}[Doubling fuel for the query count]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_queryFuel}
\label{Complexity.ladner_queryFuel}
\leanok

Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with components $\pi_1(z),\pi_2(z)$ of a string $z$ (both empty if $z$ is not a pair), and let $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ denote the canonical little-endian binary expansion of $n$. For a string $C$, the query fuel $F(C)$ is the one-bit string $1$ if
$\pi_1(C)$ is empty, and $\mathrm{bin}(|\pi_1(C)|)$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

For a string $C$ let $F(C)$ be $1$ if $\pi_1(C)$ is empty and
$\mathrm{bin}(|\pi_1(C)|)$ otherwise. Then $|F(C)|=\ell(|\pi_1(C)|)+1$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{Complexity.ladner_countInit}
\label{Complexity.ladner_countInit}
\leanok

Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with first component
$\pi_1$, and let $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ denote the canonical little-endian binary expansion of $n$. For a string $C$, with $F(C)$ the one-bit string $1$ if $\pi_1(C)$ is
empty and $\mathrm{bin}(|\pi_1(C)|)$ otherwise, the initial count state is
$\langle C,\langle F(C),\varepsilon\rangle\rangle$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One doubling round of the query count]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_countStep}
\label{Complexity.ladner_countStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with components $\pi_1(z),\pi_2(z)$ of a string $z$ (both empty if $z$ is not a pair). For a state $S$ put $C=\pi_1(S)$, $r=\pi_1(\pi_2(S))$, $a=\pi_2(\pi_2(S))$ and
$a'=a\,a\,1$. The doubling round returns $S$ if $r$ is empty, and otherwise returns
$\langle C,\langle r',b\rangle\rangle$, where $r'$ is $r$ without its first bit and $b=a'$ if
$|a'|\le 2(|C|+1)$, $b=a$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The candidate test is polynomial-time]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_candidate_FP}
\label{Complexity.ladner_candidate_FP}

Suppose there is a language $V\in\mathsf P$ such that for every Boolean string $x$, $x\in\mathrm{SAT}$ if and only if $xu\in V$ for some Boolean string $u$ with $|u|=|x|+1$. Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with components $\pi_1(z),\pi_2(z)$ of a string $z$ (both empty if $z$ is not a pair), let $\mathrm{val}(w)$ denote the value of a little-endian binary word $w$, $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$), and $M_i$ denote the machine decoded from the binary digits of $i$ by the fixed uniform machine code, where $M_i$ is said to accept $x$ within $t$ steps if it halts on $x$ within $t$ steps with output the single bit $1$; the memo values of a string $T$ are the numbers whose little-endian binary expansions are the successive first components obtained by repeatedly splitting $T$ as a pair and continuing with the second component until the remainder is empty; for a list $v$ of natural numbers, $\mathrm{SAT}_v$ is the set of strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{v_{|\psi|}}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$, where $v_m$ is read as $0$ when $m$ is out of range; and the candidate bit $\chi(C)$ of a string $C$ is $1$ exactly when, with $n=|\pi_1(C)|$, $i=\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(C)))$ and $v$ the memo values of $\pi_2(\pi_2(C))$, the list $v$ has length $n$, $i<\ell(\ell(n))$, and for every Boolean string $x$ with $|x|\le\ell(n)$, $M_i$ accepts $x$ within $i\,|x|^i$ steps if and only if $x\in\mathrm{SAT}_v$. string $C$ to the one-bit string $\chi(C)$ is computable in polynomial time.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Candidate context for a memo table]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_selectCtx}
\label{Complexity.ladner_selectCtx}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_values, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings and $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ denote the canonical little-endian binary expansion of $n$; the memo
values of a string $T$ are the numbers whose binary expansions are the successive first
components obtained by repeatedly splitting $T$ as a pair. For a string $T$ with $k$ memo values
and $i\in\mathbb N$, the candidate context is $\langle 1^{k},\langle\mathrm{bin}(i),T\rangle\rangle$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Initial selection state]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_selectInit}
\label{Complexity.ladner_selectInit}
\leanok
\uses{Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings. For a string $T$, the
initial selection state is $\langle T,\langle\varepsilon,\langle\varepsilon,\varepsilon\rangle\rangle\rangle$,
recording the table, an empty unary rank and an empty completion flag.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One round of stage selection]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_selectStep}
\label{Complexity.ladner_selectStep}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_candidate, Complexity.ladner_selectCtx, Complexity.ladner_values, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with components $\pi_1(z),\pi_2(z)$ of a string $z$ (both empty if $z$ is not a pair), let $\mathrm{val}(w)$ denote the value of a little-endian binary word $w$, $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ denote the canonical little-endian binary expansion of $n$, $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$), and $M_i$ denote the machine decoded from the binary digits of $i$ by the fixed uniform machine code, where $M_i$ is said to accept $x$ within $t$ steps if it halts on $x$ within $t$ steps with output the single bit $1$; the memo values of a string $T$ are the numbers whose little-endian binary expansions are the successive first components obtained by repeatedly splitting $T$ as a pair and continuing with the second component until the remainder is empty; for a list $v$ of natural numbers, $\mathrm{SAT}_v$ is the set of strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{v_{|\psi|}}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$, where $v_m$ is read as $0$ when $m$ is out of range; and the candidate bit $\chi(C)$ of a string $C$ is $1$ exactly when, with $n=|\pi_1(C)|$, $i=\mathrm{val}(\pi_1(\pi_2(C)))$ and $v$ the memo values of $\pi_2(\pi_2(C))$, the list $v$ has length $n$, $i<\ell(\ell(n))$, and for every Boolean string $x$ with $|x|\le\ell(n)$, $M_i$ accepts $x$ within $i\,|x|^i$ steps if and only if $x\in\mathrm{SAT}_v$. Finally,
the selection round $\lambda$ acts on a state $S$ as follows: put $T=\pi_1(S)$, let $k$ be the number of memo values of $T$, and put $\rho=\pi_1(\pi_2(S))$ (the rank), $f=\pi_1(\pi_2(\pi_2(S)))$ (the flag) and $c=\ell(\ell(k))$ (the cap); then $\lambda(S)=S$ if $f$ is nonempty; otherwise, if $|\rho|<c$, $\lambda(S)$ is $\langle T,\langle\rho,\langle 1,\mathrm{bin}(|\rho|)\rangle\rangle\rangle$ when $\chi(\langle 1^{k},\langle\mathrm{bin}(|\rho|),T\rangle\rangle)=1$ and $\langle T,\langle\rho1,\langle\varepsilon,\varepsilon\rangle\rangle\rangle$ when it is $0$; and if $|\rho|\ge c$, $\lambda(S)=\langle T,\langle\rho,\langle 1,\mathrm{bin}(c)\rangle\rangle\rangle$.
\end{definition}

a completed selection state.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[One memo-table extension]

Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with components $\pi_1(z),\pi_2(z)$ of a string $z$ (both empty if $z$ is not a pair), let $\mathrm{bin}(n)$ denote the canonical little-endian binary expansion of $n$, $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$), and $M_i$ denote the machine decoded from the binary digits of $i$ by the fixed uniform machine code, where $M_i$ is said to accept $x$ within $t$ steps if it halts on $x$ within $t$ steps with output the single bit $1$; the memo values of a string $T$ are the numbers whose little-endian binary expansions are the successive first components obtained by repeatedly splitting $T$ as a pair and continuing with the second component until the remainder is empty; for a list $v$ of natural numbers, $\mathrm{SAT}_v$ is the set of strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{v_{|\psi|}}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$, where $v_m$ is read as $0$ when $m$ is out of range; and for a list $v$ of natural numbers of length $k$, the stage value $s(v)$ is the least $i<\ell(\ell(k))$ such that for every Boolean string $x$ with $|x|\le\ell(k)$, $M_i$ accepts $x$ within $i\,|x|^i$ steps if and only if $x\in\mathrm{SAT}_v$, and $s(v)=\ell(\ell(k))$ if there is no such $i$. to $\langle\pi_1(S),\,\pi_2(S)\,\langle\mathrm{bin}(s(v)),\varepsilon\rangle\rangle$, where $v$ is
the list of memo values of $\pi_2(S)$ and the second component is the concatenation of
$\pi_2(S)$ with $\langle\mathrm{bin}(s(v)),\varepsilon\rangle$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Verifier for padded SAT]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_verifier}
\label{Complexity.ladner_verifier}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_parse, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with components $\pi_1(z),\pi_2(z)$ of a string $z$ (both empty if $z$ is not a pair). For a function $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and a language $V$ of Boolean strings, the padded
verifier language consists of the strings $S$ such that $\pi_1(S)=p\,0\,1^t$, with $p$ the prefix
before the last $0$ of $\pi_1(S)$, where $t=|p|^{h(|p|)}$, $|\pi_2(S)|=|p|+1$ and
$p\,\pi_2(S)\in V$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[The padded verifier is in P]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_verifier_P}
\label{Complexity.ladner_verifier_P}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.BinArith.polyTimeComputable_slot2, Complexity.P, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.append, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.inter_mem_P, Complexity.ladner_padSyntax, Complexity.ladner_parse, Complexity.ladner_parseWord, Complexity.ladner_parse_FP, Complexity.ladner_syntax_FP, Complexity.ladner_verifier, Complexity.lenEq_preimage_mem_P, Complexity.mem_P_of_test, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_const, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairSndD, Complexity.preimage_mem_P}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, with components $\pi_1(z),\pi_2(z)$ of a string $z$ (both empty if $z$ is not a pair). Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be such that $x\mapsto\mathrm{bin}(h(|x|))$, the binary
expansion of $h$ at the length of a Boolean string, is polynomial-time computable, and let
$V\in\mathsf P$. Then the language of strings $S$ such that $\pi_1(S)=p\,0\,1^t$ with $p$ the
prefix before the last $0$, $t=|p|^{h(|p|)}$, $|\pi_2(S)|=|p|+1$ and $p\,\pi_2(S)\in V$ belongs to
$\mathsf P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Padded membership via the verifier]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_verifier_equiv}
\label{Complexity.ladner_verifier_equiv}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.SAT, Complexity.ladner_pad_membership, Complexity.ladner_parse, Complexity.ladner_parsed_length, Complexity.ladner_verifier, Complexity.padSAT, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\langle u,v\rangle$ be the self-delimiting pairing of Boolean strings, $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$,
and $\mathrm{SAT}_h$ is the set of strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$. Let $V$ be a language such that for every Boolean string $x$, $x\in\mathrm{SAT}$ if and
only if $xu\in V$ for some $u$ with $|u|=|x|+1$, and let $W$ be the set of strings
$\langle y,u\rangle$ such that $y=p\,0\,1^t$ with $p$ the prefix before the last $0$ of $y$,
$t=|p|^{h(|p|)}$, $|u|=|p|+1$ and $pu\in V$. Then for every Boolean string $y$,
$y\in\mathrm{SAT}_h$ if and only if there is $u$ with $|u|\le|y|+1$ and $\langle y,u\rangle\in W$.
\end{theorem}

string to the binary expansion of $h$ at its length, is polynomial-time computable, and let
$\mathrm{SAT}_h$ is the set of strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$. Then $\mathrm{SAT}_h\in\mathsf{NP}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Literal padded word]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_padWord}
\label{Complexity.ladner_padWord}
\leanok
For a function $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and a Boolean string $x$, the padded word of $x$ is
$x\,0\,1^{|x|^{h(|x|)}}$: the string $x$, a separator bit $0$, and $|x|^{h(|x|)}$ ones.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Bounded exponents give polynomial padding length]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_bounded_pad_length}
\label{Complexity.ladner_bounded_pad_length}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.ladner_padWord}
\difficulty{4}
Let $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and $C\in\mathbb N$ with $h(n)\le C$ for all $n$. Then for every
Boolean string $x$, the padded word $x\,0\,1^{|x|^{h(|x|)}}$ has length at most
$2(|x|+1)^{C+1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The Ladner language is outside P]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_outside_P}
\label{Complexity.ladner_outside_P}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.P, Complexity.P_eq_NP_of_NPHard_mem_P, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.SAT_H, Complexity.SAT_H_eq, Complexity.SAT_NPHard, Complexity.ladnerH, Complexity.ladner_bounded_pad_reduction, Complexity.mem_P_of_polyTimeReducible}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$) and $M_i$ denote the machine decoded from the binary digits of $i$ by the fixed uniform machine code, where $M_i$ is said to accept $x$ within $t$ steps if it halts on $x$ within $t$ steps with output the single bit $1$. Let $H$ be Ladner's delayed index function, where $H(n)$ is the least $i<\ell(\ell(n))$ such that for every Boolean string $x$ with $|x|\le\ell(n)$, $M_i$ accepts $x$ within $i\,|x|^i$ steps if and only if $x\in\mathrm{SAT}_H$, and $H(n)=\ell(\ell(n))$ if there is no such $i$; here $\mathrm{SAT}_H$ is the set of strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{H(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$. Suppose $\mathsf P\ne\mathsf{NP}$, the map
$x\mapsto\mathrm{bin}(H(|x|))$ (the binary expansion of $H$ at the length of a Boolean string) is
polynomial-time computable, and $\mathrm{SAT}_H\in\mathsf P$ would imply that there is a constant
$C$ with $H(n)\le C$ for all $n$. Then $\mathrm{SAT}_H\notin\mathsf P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The Ladner language is not NP-complete]
\lean{Complexity.ladner_not_complete}
\label{Complexity.ladner_not_complete}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.NP, Complexity.NPComplete, Complexity.NPComplete_iff, Complexity.NPHard, Complexity.P, Complexity.P_eq_NP_of_NPHard_mem_P, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.SAT, Complexity.SAT_H, Complexity.SAT_H_eq, Complexity.SAT_NPHard, Complexity.ladnerH, Complexity.padSAT}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\ell(n)=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor$ (with $\ell(0)=0$) and $M_i$ denote the machine decoded from the binary digits of $i$ by the fixed uniform machine code, where $M_i$ is said to accept $x$ within $t$ steps if it halts on $x$ within $t$ steps with output the single bit $1$. Let $H$ be Ladner's delayed index function, where $H(n)$ is the least $i<\ell(\ell(n))$ such that for every Boolean string $x$ with $|x|\le\ell(n)$, $M_i$ accepts $x$ within $i\,|x|^i$ steps if and only if $x\in\mathrm{SAT}_H$, and $H(n)=\ell(\ell(n))$ if there is no such $i$; here $\mathrm{SAT}_H$ is the set of strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{H(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$. Suppose that $\mathsf P\ne\mathsf{NP}$; that the map
$x\mapsto\mathrm{bin}(H(|x|))$, sending a Boolean string to the binary expansion of $H$ at its
length, is polynomial-time computable; that $\mathrm{SAT}_H\notin\mathsf P$;
that $\mathrm{SAT}_H\notin\mathsf P$ implies that for every $C$ there is $N$ with $C\le H(n)$ for
all $n\ge N$; and that for every $h:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ with $x\mapsto\mathrm{bin}(h(|x|))$
polynomial-time computable and such that for every $C$ there is $N$ with $C\le h(n)$ for all
$n\ge N$, $\mathsf{NP}$-hardness of the language
$\mathrm{SAT}_h$ of strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{h(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$ implies
$\mathrm{SAT}\in\mathsf P$. Then $\mathrm{SAT}_H$ is not $\mathsf{NP}$-complete.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[The Ladner language is NP-intermediate]

\leanok

Let $H$ be Ladner's delayed index function, where $H(n)$ is the least $i<\ell(\ell(n))$ such that for every Boolean string $x$ with $|x|\le\ell(n)$, $M_i$ accepts $x$ within $i\,|x|^i$ steps if and only if $x\in\mathrm{SAT}_H$, and $H(n)=\ell(\ell(n))$ if there is no such $i$; here $\mathrm{SAT}_H$ is the set of strings $\psi\,0\,1^{|\psi|^{H(|\psi|)}}$ with $\psi\in\mathrm{SAT}$.
